subject: POC eval modality, timeline & grading rubric — proposed next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@optimahealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next: POC evaluation approach and success criteria

Hi Marissa / Ben / Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on where OptimaHealth wants to go. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get the POC scoped: 

- Primary objective: reduce triage time for clinical support agents by surfacing an accurate recommended action and a confidence score.
- Success signals we care about: suggestion accuracy (top-1), false-positive rate (safety/hallucination), and end-to-end latency under 400ms for 95th pct.

We discussed two evaluation routes: 1) online shadowing (run Redwood inference in parallel on live traffic) and 2) offline scoring (sampled historical logs scored by clinicians). Our preference is to move quickly — can you propose a concrete plan that 1) balances risk and speed, 2) defines measurable success gates, and 3) assigns owners and timeline?

Also include any instrumentation requirements and a minimal acceptance rubric so we can review internally before kickoff.

Thanks — I can loop in procurement once we have a scope and cost estimate.

Samira
VP Product, OptimaHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@optimahealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next: POC evaluation approach and success criteria

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a compact POC charter and a proposed grading rubric (attached) — high level plan below.

Proposed evaluation modality (hybrid timebox):
- Week 0 (prep, 3–5 business days): instrumentation + sample selection. Owner: Ben (engineering). Deliverables: request/response logging hook, latency traces, sample export (2,000 anonymized cases).
- Weeks 1–2 (shadow, 10 business days): run Redwood in shadow mode on a subset of live traffic (10–15% sampling) to validate latency and surfaced outputs without user impact. Owner: Marissa / OptimaHealth engineering contact (Dan).
- Week 3 (offline scoring, 5 business days): clinical team scores a stratified sample of ~2,000 items (mix of high/low confidence). We provide an offline grading UI and an initial rubric. Owner: OptimaHealth clinical lead (TBD) + Redwood CS for scoring support.

Acceptance gates (must pass at least 2 of 3):
1) Top-1 suggestion accuracy >= 78% (clinician-scored)
2) Hallucination/false-positive rate <= 6% on clinician review
3) 95th pct latency < 400ms in shadow (with 95% of requests served from warmed KV cache)

Scoring rubric highlights (see attached eval-grading-rubric-v2.xlsx):
- Primary metric: top-1 accuracy (weight 0.5)
- Safety/hallucination: (weight 0.25) — binary flag per response + impact severity
- Confidence calibration & NER correctness: (weight 0.15)
- Latency/ops: (weight 0.10) — bucketed scoring for p50/p95

Next steps / asks for OptimaHealth:
- Confirm owner for clinical scoring (name + point of contact).
- Approve the instrumentation checklist (attached) and give Dan permission to add hooks to the sandbox environment.
- Agree to the hybrid timebox above or propose a change.

I attached: optima-poc-charter-v1.pdf, eval-grading-rubric-v2.xlsx, instrumentation-checklist.md. Also linking a short Kickoff doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcDefGhy-poc-charter.

If that looks good I will: create the JIRA ticket, schedule a 30-minute kickoff next week, and send a short SOW for procurement.

—Marissa
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@optimahealth.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next: POC evaluation approach and success criteria

Adding a few technical clarifications and commitments from infra/eng: 

- Instrumentation: we need an authenticated sandbox endpoint and a header to carry a stable request-id. See checklist I attached. Minimal logging fields: request_id, timestamp, model_variant, latency_ms, input_hash, top_k_responses, confidence_scores. Optima should be able to drop PHI in the sandbox export; we'll provide helper scripts.
- Shadow load: start at 5% of a single routing key, verify p95 latency, then scale to 10–15% if p95 is within target. We'll keep a warm pool to reduce cold starts.
- Sampling for offline scoring: propose stratified sampling by confidence decile (200 samples per decile) to target edge cases. That yields 2,000 items.

Operational owners & tasks:
- Ben (engineering): instrumentation + deployment of shadow route (JIRA-RED-9213). ETA: week 0 complete.
- Marissa (CS): clinical scoring coordination and weekly checkpoints.
- Rishi (solutions/ML): select model variant and quantization profile; run initial offline baseline tests (compare open-llm-v3-medium vs optima-tuned-1).

I'll create the JIRA ticket and attach the instrumentation checklist. If Optima wants, we can run an initial 1-day smoke shadow test to validate pipeline and logs before the 2-week run.

—Ben
Senior Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@optimahealth.ai>

Marissa / Ben — this looks good and pragmatic. We can confirm the clinical scoring owner as Dr. Alicia Perez; I'll introduce her on the kickoff. Procurement flagged that they need the SOW and an initial estimate to start the review — could you share the SOW draft and a ballpark cost by end of the week? Also Dan will scope the sandbox access and add the header Ben requested.

We are happy to start with the 5% smoke shadow next Tuesday and run the 2-week shadow the following week. Please schedule the 30-minute kickoff for Monday morning if possible — Dr. Perez will join.

Thanks — Samira
VP Product, OptimaHealth
